Plotting after the 0.2.4 API consolidation

Source: R/help_plot_migration.R
mfrmr_plot_migration.Rd

Use plot() on a fitted model or an analysis result. The 33 former drawing helpers are no longer exported in 0.2.4. This is a breaking API change: replace old plot_*() calls using the table below. Their numerical/drawing implementations remain internal; do not depend on mfrmr::: access. The public data accessors plot_data() and plot_data_components() remain.

Choosing an input

Use a fitted ordinary model for fit-level views. Use saved G/D studies, information, DIF/DFF, bias, QC or PCA results for their own plot() methods. Their public help pages explain the view controls, returned tables and interpretation: plot.mfrm_information(), plot.mfrm_dif(), plot.mfrm_dif_interaction(), plot.mfrm_anchor_drift(), plot.mfrm_qc_pipeline(), plot.mfrm_bias(), plot.mfrm_residual_pca() and plot.mfrm_diagnostics(). plot.mfrm_population_intervals() adds saved latent-regression coefficients and contrasts. Start with these pages for saved results. A common function name does not make every view available for every model. Two-family GPCM and corrected JML retain their separate supported result routes. Plotting does not add intervals, repair unavailable values or equate scales. Use original result objects rather than unclassed lists or CSV tables.

Single-fit views

plot(fit) still draws the ordinary Wright map. New type choices include reliability, agreement, person_fit, rater_severity, thresholds, residual_qq, residual_matrix, residual_pca, local_dependence, marginal_fit, marginal_pairwise, fair_average, displacement, facets_chisq, bubble, guttman, unexpected, qc, apa_summary, bias, facet_equivalence and facet_dashboard.

Use metric for the quantity and view for a display variant. Reliability accepts reliability, separation or strata. Agreement accepts exact or correlation, with view = "pairs" (default) or "heatmap"; metric = "difference" applies only to pairs. Severity separation is not agreement. The former plot_type argument becomes view for marginal fit, fair averages, displacement, facet chi-square, unexpected ratings and facet dashboards. Keep other named controls from the legacy parameter help.

Explicit controls are passed only to the chosen renderer; omitted controls retain that renderer's defaults. Inapplicable and conflicting controls are rejected. Supply matching saved diagnostics for repeated fit-level views. Some legacy fit-level convenience routes compute diagnostics when omitted; this does not imply model refitting. Saved-result plots reuse their results.

Replacement table

In the table, x is the former first argument, including its original result class. For paired models use reference and comparison. For an ordered trajectory, fits is the existing named list of fitted models.

Former exported helperReplacement
plot_anchor_drift()plot(x)
plot_apa_figure_one()plot(x, type = "apa_summary")
plot_bias_interaction()plot(x, type = "bias")
plot_bubble()plot(x, type = "bubble")
plot_compare_mfrm()plot(reference, comparison = comparison)
plot_dif_heatmap()plot(x, type = "heatmap")
plot_dif_summary()plot(x, type = "summary")
plot_displacement()plot(x, type = "displacement")
plot_facet_equivalence()plot(x, type = "facet_equivalence")
plot_facet_quality_dashboard()plot(x, type = "facet_dashboard")
plot_facets_chisq()plot(x, type = "facets_chisq")
plot_fair_average()plot(x, type = "fair_average")
plot_guttman_scalogram()plot(x, type = "guttman")
plot_information()plot(x)
plot_interrater_agreement()plot(x, type = "agreement")
plot_local_dependence_heatmap()plot(x, type = "local_dependence")
plot_marginal_fit()plot(x, type = "marginal_fit")
plot_marginal_pairwise()plot(x, type = "marginal_pairwise")
plot_person_fit()plot(x, type = "person_fit")
plot_qc_dashboard()plot(x, type = "qc")
plot_qc_pipeline()plot(x)
plot_rater_agreement_heatmap()plot(x, type = "agreement", view = "heatmap")
plot_rater_severity_profile()plot(x, type = "rater_severity")
plot_rater_trajectory()plot((fits)[[1L]], type = "trajectory", comparison = (fits)[-1L], labels = names(fits))
plot_reliability_snapshot()plot(x, type = "reliability")
plot_residual_matrix()plot(x, type = "residual_matrix")
plot_residual_pca()plot(x, type = "residual_pca")
plot_residual_qq()plot(x, type = "residual_qq")
plot_response_time_review()plot(x)
plot_shrinkage_funnel()plot(x, type = "shrinkage", view = "funnel")
plot_threshold_ladder()plot(x, type = "thresholds")
plot_unexpected()plot(x, type = "unexpected")
plot_wright_unified()plot(x, type = "wright", view = "unified")

For result objects the object determines the target: for example plot(info, type = "iif", facet = "Rater") or plot(dif, type = "heatmap", metric = "contrast"). For the fit convenience routes, rename the old bias plot argument to view; rename the old equivalence type to view. For residual PCA rename plot_type to view with type = "residual_pca", or use plot(pca, type = "loadings") directly on a saved PCA result.

Multiple models and occasions

Use plot(reference, comparison = other, type = "ccc") or type = "wright" for paired displays; view = "difference" shows differences without adding difference SEs or model-selection tests. For trajectories use plot(fits[[1]], type = "trajectory", comparison = fits[-1], labels = names(fits)). Labels include the first model, and the supplied order is retained. Models must already be placed on an interpretable common scale; plotting performs no linking.

Returned data and appearance

Use draw = FALSE to obtain the existing payload without drawing. Most routes return mfrm_plot_data; the QC pipeline retains its verdict-table return, and native interval routes retain their existing ggplot results. Return classes have not been homogenized. Use plot_data() for supported payloads and as_ggplot() only for supported conversions. Unsupported conversions do not become available through this API change. Titles and cautions stay outside figures by default; keep returned notes when exporting. G/D plots retain their existing color, monochrome, score and facet-panel controls. Save full result objects for later plotting.
